entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Wen Zhengming, born Wen Bi (文璧), was a renowned Chinese painter, calligrapher, and poet during the Ming dynasty. He was regarded as one of the Four Masters of Ming painting, a group of four artists who dominated the art scene in the 16th century.

Wen Zhengming's artistic career spanned several decades, during which he created numerous works of art that showcased his expertise in both traditional Chinese techniques and innovative methods.

His most famous works include his landscapes and portraits, which often featured meticulous attention to detail and a deep understanding of the human condition.

Wen Zhengming's legacy extends beyond his own art, as he played a significant role in shaping the artistic landscape of the Ming dynasty and influencing future generations of Chinese artists.

"The lotus flower blooms in the muddiest of waters yet remains unsoiled," Wen Zhengming once said, "A true artist must cultivate a sense of inner peace and clarity, even in the face of adversity." This quote encapsulates the essence of Wen Zhengming's artistic philosophy and continues to inspire artists to this day.

Wen Zhengming died on March 28, 1559, at the age of 70, leaving behind a legacy of breathtaking beauty and artistic innovation.
